C50.question: Does §9.4's Open Vault league ship at launch, and if it does, does a block remove two Open Vault players from each other's targets?
C50.why_it_matters: §17.8 keeps a blocked player's island in the target pool because 'a raid takes nothing', which is false in the Open Vault league, where loot leaves the defender. The league has no screen, no build and no task, and its central rule is missing: §9.4 removed the percentages that said what a raid takes. §26.1 lists it neither at launch nor after, while §19.21 and §27.5 have soft launch report both leagues.
C50.today: Nothing of the league is built: server/, sim/ and client/ have no Open Vault (a grep finds only sim/src/replay.rs's unrelated 'open Vault'), and no roadmap task builds it. Blocking is built as §17.8 says (server/src/safety.mjs:10-16): it hides each player from the other in Workshop lists and the feed, ends a friendship, closes invites and challenge links, and leaves both islands as targets. Screens v3's block sheet repeats §17.8's reason, 'Your islands can still meet as raid targets, because a raid takes nothing' (screens_meta.js:1284), and its League tab has no Open Vault.

options.label: Move the league after launch
options.means: Launch has one-way theft only. §9.4 says the Open Vault league comes after launch, §26.1 lists it among the after-launch modes, and §19.21 and §27.5 stop promising that soft launch reports both. Its rules (what a raid takes, who meets whom, blocking, minors) are written before it is scheduled.
options.consequences: §17.8 is true at launch with no edit. Nothing waits on it: §19.21 already keeps one-way theft the default whatever the two leagues show. Players who want real stakes wait for a later version.
options.doc_edit: §9.4: 'Players who want real stakes will be able to opt into the Open Vault league after launch (26.1), …'. §26.1, Modes, after launch: add 'the Open Vault league'. §19.21's One-way theft row and §27.5: 'soft launch reports both' becomes 'the Open Vault league follows launch (26.1)'. §17.8 unchanged.
options.build_change: None: nothing is built. The roadmap gains a post-launch task that starts by writing the league's rules.

options.label: At launch; a block parts Open Vault players
options.means: The league opens at launch, joined from the League tab (§23.2). §17.8 gains: in the Open Vault league a raid does take, so a block removes each player from the other's Open Vault targets; one-way raids between them are unchanged. The document first writes what a raid takes, who is matched with whom, whether 13-to-15s may join and how often a player may switch.
options.consequences: Soft launch reports both leagues, as §27.5 says. Within that league, blocking can shrink a player's pool and dodge a strong defender, the abuse §17.8 names. One developer builds a second loot rule before launch: a debit from the defender, the 40% uplift, a matchmaking pool, the economy model's flows and a screen.
options.numbers: Rewards 40% higher on both sides (§9.4). Sealed share 40% at Vault level 1 to 71.5% at level 10 (§9.4). Up to 500 blocks a player (safety.mjs MOST_BLOCKS).
options.doc_edit: §17.8: the sentence above. §9.4: what an Open Vault raid takes and who meets whom. §23.2's League tab: the opt-in. §20.7: an Open Vault row by age band.
options.build_change: server: an Open Vault flag on accounts, matchmaking inside the pool, the defender's debit and the 40% uplift at settlement, and the block filter on Open Vault targets; tools/economy_model: the league's flows; client: the opt-in on the League tab.

options.label: At launch; a block changes nothing in either league
options.means: As B, but §17.8's rule holds in both leagues and its reason no longer rests on 'a raid takes nothing': targets are chosen by matchmaking, not by players, and letting blocking remove them would shrink the pool and let players dodge strong defenders.
options.consequences: One blocking rule for both leagues and none of the dodging §17.8 warns of. A player can still be raided, with real loss, by someone they blocked, though only if matchmaking pairs them and with no names while it runs; leaving the league is their way out. The build work is B's, less the block filter.
options.numbers: As B.
options.doc_edit: §17.8, second paragraph: 'Their island can still appear as a target, and yours as theirs, in both leagues. Targets are chosen by matchmaking, never by a player, and raids are anonymous while they happen; in the Open Vault league a raid does take, and a player who wants no such risk can leave it.' B's §9.4, §23.2 and §20.7 edits.
options.build_change: As B, without the block filter.

recommendation.rationale: Nothing of the league exists, and it lacks its central rule: §9.4 removed the percentages that said what leaves the defender, so B and C must write and build a second economy before launch, for one developer. §19.21 and §27.5 already say nothing waits on comparing the leagues, so moving it costs launch nothing, and §17.8 then holds as written. When the league is scheduled, B's block rule is the one to write with it; C keeps one rule at the cost of a blocker's protection.

quotes.text: This looks odd until you remember that a raid takes nothing: there is no harm to be protected from, and raids are anonymous while they happen.
Players who want real stakes opt into the Open Vault league, where the rules below apply in full and rewards are 40% higher on both sides.
The percentages this paragraph used to carry are gone: they described a world where the loot left the defender, and it does not.
soft launch reports both and nothing waits on the comparison (27.5)

C50.also_needed: Under A, which version brings the league. Under B or C, what an Open Vault raid takes from the defender, whether Open Vault players meet only each other, whether 13-to-15s may join (§20.2 gives them no rule for real loss), and how often a player may join or leave.

C51.question: Which first session does the document keep: §16's heist at 2:00 after §23.5's set-up with §25.2's target restated, §16 shortened so the heist starts within 45 seconds, or the heist moved before everything but the age check?
C51.why_it_matters: §15.2, §16 and §25.2 give three times for the first heist and two answers on whether minute one is guided, so the first launch cannot be built (TD.26) or measured against §25.2's funnel until one wins. §25.2 forbids prompts and account creation before the first heist, while §20.1's platform age check is a system prompt and §23.5 adopts the Keeper's name before play. Under §5.6's 10 minutes, §16's Half gravity woven at 0:30 and Bloom at 6:30 would leave their slots empty until 10:30 and 16:30, past the session's 10:00 end.
C51.today: No first session is built. The client opens on §20.1's age check and keeps the answer on the phone (client/scripts/age_screen.gd, client/data/age_check.gd); home then signs in when online, and the server makes the account, holding it at 13 to 15 until the band arrives (server/src/service.mjs:151-158). There is no tutorial ruin, beat or Keeper name and no weaving time; the island builder weaves at once (client/scripts/builder_screen.gd:149). TD.26 builds §23.5's order last. Screens v3's first launch runs the title, a system sheet 'Share your age range?' (markup 439), the protections, the Keeper's name and face, then §16's beats at §16's times (0:00 to 10:00), the heist at 2:00, a pointing hand on every beat, and weaves at once.

options.label: §16's clock, §25.2 restated (the design's order)
options.means: Title, the age check, the protections, the Keeper's name and face, then §16 as written: Half gravity woven at 0:30, the crew at 1:15, the first heist at 2:00. §25.2's median time to the first heist is counted from the end of the age check, with a figure this order reaches. §15.2's first heist moves to minute 2 and is unguided, with its hint after two failed escapes; the design's pointing hand appears only as §15.1's hint after failure.
options.consequences: Keeps §23.5's adopted order, §16's teaching order and Screens v3's times, so only §25.2's figure and two §15.2 cells change. The 45-second target goes: the first heist comes at about two and a half minutes, and §25.2's 95% reach is measured over that longer path.
options.numbers: §16: heist at 2:00 from 0:00. The protections and the name before 0:00: an estimated 30 seconds, so about 2:30 from the end of the age check, to be measured in soft launch.
options.doc_edit: §25.2: 'Median time to the first heist | Under 2 minutes 30 seconds from the end of the age check'; the 'Playing within 30 seconds' row: 'No account creation, no settings and no logos that can't be skipped before the first heist; the age check (20.1) is the one prompt, and the Keeper's name stays on the phone until the account is made after the first heist'. §15.2: 'Minute 1 | A guided first heist in a ruin' becomes 'Minute 2 | The first heist, in a Drifting ruin (16)', and the Half gravity row moves to minute 1. §16: 'The first session's weaves are instant; 5.6's times start after it.'
options.build_change: TD.26 in this order: the first heist runs on the phone, and platform sign-in makes the account after it, with the name; the tutorial's weaves skip §5.6's timer once weaving times are built.

options.label: §16 shortened to a 45-second heist
options.means: A's order and §16's teaching order, with the first beats shortened so the heist starts by 0:45: the page caught and woven by 0:20, the three ruleborn shown at the ruin's edge, the heist at 0:45. §25.2's 45 seconds is counted from §16's 0:00, the first beat after the Keeper's name. §15.2 and the weaves as in A.
options.consequences: §25.2's figure and §23.5's order both hold. Three lessons (a law, a weave, three abilities) are pressed into 45 seconds, and the abilities are shown mostly inside the heist. Screens v3's beat times change from 0:30, 1:15 and 2:00.
options.numbers: Heist by 0:45 from §16's 0:00, against 2:00 today. The age check, the protections and the name come before and are not counted.
options.doc_edit: §16's table re-timed: 0:00 the page, 0:20 woven, 0:30 the crew, 0:45 the first heist; the later rows unchanged. §25.2: 'Under 45 seconds, counted from the first beat after the Keeper's name', with A's prompt row. §15.2 and §16's weave sentence as in A.
options.build_change: As A, with the shorter beats.

options.label: Heist first

It reverses §23.5's adopted order, Screens v3's flow and §16's lesson order: the first law met is the ruin's Slow rivers, not a page the player catches. The protections apply from the age check but are summarised only after the heist.
options.numbers: First heist within 45 seconds of opening the app, with only the age check before it.
options.doc_edit: §23.5's first-launch row: 'Title, the age-band check, the first heist, then a summary of the protections, the Keeper's name and face, and the rest of 16'. §16's table re-ordered and re-timed with the heist first. §15.2: 'A guided first heist' becomes 'An unguided first heist'. A's §25.2 prompt row and §16 weave sentence.
options.build_change: TD.26 in this order; the design's first-launch screens are re-sequenced.

quotes.text: A guided first heist in a ruin
The first minute is unguided play
No account creation, no permission prompts, no settings and no logos that can't be skipped before the first heist.
While a slot is being woven it is empty.

C51.also_needed: §16's first experiment is suggested at 6:30, takes 5 minutes and finishes at 10:00, so it needs an earlier start or a shorter first experiment. The Keeper's name rule and where the terms are accepted (G58).

G58.question: Which rules cover how an age band changes, the play-time reminder, every Keeper's name (a word-list name at every age, or typed) and where consent and the terms are taken: the build's and the design's readings, a protective set, or the protective band rule with the design's other choices?
G58.why_it_matters: PUT /v1/age stores any band at any time, so a modified client can lift a 13-to-15's chat, spending, night and Workshop protections with one call. Screens v3 lets a 16-to-17 switch the play-time reminder off, draws it as a daily limit, and shows a 13-to-15's typed name to every raider while telling them their profile stays private. §20.5's consent by country and §20.11's terms gate have no place in the first launch, and the server asks for the terms only before Workshop actions.
G58.today: PUT /v1/age (server/src/http.mjs:528-537) deletes an under-13 account and stores any other band at once, looser or not (server/src/workshop.mjs:89-93). A new account is held at 13 to 15 until the device sends its band (server/src/service.mjs:151-158). The client asks once and keeps the answer (client/data/age_check.gd); the platforms' age services are not wired. No play-time reminder is built (accounts.reminder_at is §14.6's daily reminder), and accounts have no Keeper name; the client names other players 'Keeper' and the first letters of their account (client/README.md:143). The terms are accepted before Workshop actions only (server/src/safety.mjs:19-22); there is no consent step, and server/declarations.md declares no parental controls. Screens v3: 'You can change it later with a parent' (markup 439); a reminder of Off, 45, 60 or 90 minutes, fixed at 60 for 13 to 15 and open, Off included, for 16 to 17, counted against the day's total ('38' minutes today, 'Pause card in 22 min', screens_meta.js:897-919); 'HOW RAIDERS SEE YOU' with a typed, filtered name at every band (markup 448).

options.label: The build's and the design's readings
options.means: The device may set any band at any time. A 16-to-17 may switch the reminder off, and it counts the day's play. Every player types a filtered name, and raiders see it at every band. The terms are accepted before Workshop actions; there is no consent step.
options.consequences: Nothing to change on the server, and Screens v3 is drawn as it is. A modified client, or a 13-to-15 who answers again, lifts every §20.2 protection. A 13-to-15's real name can reach raiders, since a filter catches words, not names, and a typed name is the free text §24.6 rules out. The reminder reads as a daily limit the document does not have, and friends, the feed and purchases run with no terms accepted.
options.doc_edit: §20.1: 'The band can be changed in Settings.' §20.2's reminder row, 16 and 17: 'Every 90 minutes by default; can be turned off', with a note that it counts the day's play. §20.11: 'the terms are accepted before a player first publishes or plays a Workshop island'.
options.build_change: None on the server for the band and the terms. A Keeper name field with a word filter in English and Brazilian Portuguese (§20.4); the reminder and the name step as designed (TD.25, TD.26).

options.label: A protective set
options.means: Band: the first answer sets any band; after it the device may only tighten it, and a looser band comes only from the platform's age service. Reminder: 13 to 15 every 60 minutes, fixed; 16 and 17 every 60 or 90, 90 by default, never off; adults off by default; it counts continuous play in one session (G29's, the app in the foreground) and shows when a heist ends. Name: every Keeper picks a name from word lists, at every age, as C43's answer does for islands, and raiders see it as §12.4's free 'name'. Terms: accepted once, when the account is made after the first heist (C51), before friends, the Workshop or a purchase.
options.consequences: A modified client cannot lift a minor's protections on a live account. A player who answers 13 to 15 by mistake, or turns 16, stays at the tighter band until the platform reports a looser one; until those services are wired, only a new account changes it. A word-list name identifies nobody, needs no filter or moderation and keeps §24.6's 'no free text', and still gives raiders §12.4's free information. The reminder is a break suggestion, never a limit.

G59.question: How is the contrast of outlined text measured: never by its outline, against an ink outline that goes all round, or against an outline or a hard drop shadow?
G59.why_it_matters: 28% of Screens v3's text runs fail §21.8's 4.5:1 or its perceptual check, so as drawn many words are hard to read, most of all for players with low vision. The design carries light words on bright fills and over the 3D world with ink strokes and hard shadows, and v3.6 does not say whether those count, so the build's check cannot pass or fail them.
G59.today: client/tests/a11y_tests.gd:58-81 measures a word against a StyleBoxFlat's fill over the day sky's two ends, by the formulas in client/ui/colour_check.gd; it knows neither gradients nor outlines. Measured over Screens v3's 1,049 text runs on 28 screens, against the pixels under each: 201 (19%) under 4.5:1, 250 (24%) under the perceptual level for their size and weight, 292 (28%) failing one or the other. The causes: white badges on red, green and violet fills (85 runs, 1.8 to 2.8:1); the law card's 'Stillness' in white on cyan (1.55:1); tertiary #8A7AA8 (Lc 34); secondary #B8A8D8 (Lc 57 to 59); light browns on parchment (3.04 to 4.22:1); crew names in school colours over the 3D ground (1.4 to 3.1:1). §23.5 lists text size, not contrast.

options.label: Outlines never count
options.means: A word is measured against what is behind it; outlines and shadows are decoration.
options.consequences: The simplest rule, but every word over the 3D world or on a busy fill needs a plate or a halo, which changes the heist's crew names and many badges from the design.
options.numbers: 292 runs (28%) to fix, including the 31 that outlines or shadows would carry.
options.doc_edit: §21.8 Type: 'Words are measured against what is behind them, at its worst point; outlines and shadows do not count.'
options.build_change: As B's token fixes, and every word over the world on a plate or halo; the check learns the colour behind each word.

options.label: An ink outline all round counts
options.means: Words with an ink outline all round, at least 1.5 points or 12% of their size wide, are measured against the outline. A drop shadow does not count. Every other word is measured against what is behind it.
options.consequences: Keeps the design's outlined words and lets the build draw light words over the 3D world with an outline, which a check can read from the label. The crew names' drop shadows become full outlines. The rest is fixed in the tokens, keeping the look.
options.numbers: As drawn, 1 of the 201 runs under 4.5:1 passes by its outline. The crew names' shadows read 5.8 to 10.3:1 against the names, so the same ink as a full outline passes.
options.doc_edit: §21.8 Type: 'Words with an ink outline all round, at least 1.5 points or 12% of their size wide, are measured against the outline; a drop shadow does not count. Other words are measured against what is behind them, at its worst point.'
options.build_change: client/ui/tokens.json: tertiary text lifted to #B8A8D8 and bold, secondary to #D8CCF2, badges with ink words or on the fill's deep end (#C42040), no opacity on words, law titles on a plate, crew names outlined (TD.3). client/tests/a11y_tests.gd learns the colour behind each word, gradients included, and reads a label's outline.

options.label: Outlines and hard shadows count
options.means: As B, and a hard ink drop shadow also counts as the background.
options.consequences: Fewest changes to the design: the crew names pass as drawn. But a drop shadow sits on one side only, so the other edges of each letter stay on the ground at 1.4 to 3.1:1.
options.numbers: 31 of the 201 runs under 4.5:1 pass as drawn: 1 by its outline, 30 by a hard shadow.
options.doc_edit: §21.8 Type as in B, with 'or a hard drop shadow' after the outline.
options.build_change: As B, and the check also reads hard shadows.

recommendation.rationale: An outline that goes all round separates each letter from whatever is behind it, which is why the design leans on it, and its width is a value a check can read. A one-sided shadow does not, so C passes words a player may not read over a light ground; A forces plates over the 3D world and moves the heist further from the design than it needs. Under B, the 4.5:1 and perceptual rules stay whole.

C52.question: Which frame-rate floor holds on which phones, and how is §24's 25 ms drag budget measured?
C52.why_it_matters: §21.3 lets the oldest supported phone fall to 30 frames a second while §24 makes 60 the floor on a mid-range Android, so a phone between them has two answers. A 60 Hz phone normally shows a drag two frames or more after the touch, so the 25 ms is missed as soon as anyone measures it, and no section says how to measure it or what a miss means.
C52.today: No client test measures frame time or drag, and the client draws no 3D yet. tools/roadmap.py's TC.8 (yours, blocked on TC.3) names §21.3's budgets and §24's 60 frames a second and 25 ms drag on the reference device, without a method. The iPhone export's minimum is iOS 15.0 and Android's minimum SDK is the engine's default (client/export_presets.cfg:27, :92). Screens v3 sets neither figure; its prototype lowers its pixel ratio when frames average over 30 ms.

options.label: Both as written
options.means: §21.3's line holds for iPhones and the oldest supported phone, §24's for the reference Android; the 25 ms stays a figure with no method.
options.consequences: Two floors for overlapping phones, and TC.8 can neither pass nor fail the drag figure.
options.numbers: One frame at 60 Hz is 16.7 ms and two are 33.3, against 25.
options.doc_edit: None
options.build_change: None

options.label: §24's device is the one rule
options.means: §21.3's frame-rate line is struck; 60 a second on the mid-range 4 GB Android at 60 Hz is the only floor. The drag budget is measured touch to picture on the reference device with a high-speed camera, one or two frames of drag prediction allowed; a miss blocks release (TC.8).
options.consequences: One rule in one place. Phones slower than the reference device, the low-end tier §24 calls the largest, get no floor at all.
options.numbers: A phone's 240-frame slow-motion video resolves about 4 ms. 25 ms is 1.5 frames at 60 Hz.
options.doc_edit: §21.3: the frame-rate line becomes 'Frame rate: see 24's reference device.' §24 Input budget: 'measured touch to picture on the reference device with a high-speed camera, with up to two frames of drag prediction; a miss blocks release'.
options.build_change: The client reads touches unaccumulated and as late as it can, predicts drags by one or two frames and keeps the 3D frame under about 8 ms; TC.8 adds frame-time and drag measures on the reference device.

options.label: One rule naming both tiers
options.means: §24's reference-device row says both: 60 a second on the reference device and anything faster, iPhone 12 and newer among them; never below 30 on the oldest supported phone, which is named. The drag budget is measured as in B. §21.3's line points to §24.
options.consequences: One home for performance, and the low-end phones keep the floor §21.3 gave them. The oldest supported phone has to be named and tested as well.
options.numbers: As B.
options.doc_edit: §24 Reference device: add '60 frames a second on it and on anything faster, iPhone 12 and newer among them; never below 30 on the oldest supported phone, named here.' Input budget as in B. §21.3: 'Frame rate: see 24's reference device.'
options.build_change: As B, and TC.8 also measures the oldest supported phone.

options.label: C, with drag counted inside the engine
options.means: Frame rule as in C. The 25 ms is counted from the engine reading the touch to handing the frame to the screen, logged by the client on the device, with no prediction and no camera.
options.consequences: A device build can measure it every time with no camera, but it leaves out the touch sensor and the display, which the research behind the 25 ms included, so passing it does not mean the drag feels as §24 intends.
options.doc_edit: As C, with the Input budget 'counted from the engine reading the touch to the frame handed to the screen'.

G48.question: No rule chooses a heist result's decisive moment or its one thing to try: write the drafted rule with the tip as the result's own 'Try this' row, keep the design's Archivist heading for the tip, or ship the design's fixed moment and tip for each outcome?
G48.why_it_matters: §12.13 makes every result name the moment that decided the heist, with a three-second replay, and one thing to try tied to it, and §23.2 makes both must-shows; but no section says how the moment is chosen, and §15.3 says only 'Based on what went wrong, never a lecture'. Which moment counts decides what a player learns from a loss, and §23.5 does not let a design add the rule. The simulation keeps no events to find it in. Your fix brief to the designer says 'plus one thing to try. Keep the Archivist card.' (screen-review.md:398), and Screens v3 heads the tip 'The Archivist · try this'. That supports option B. Intent, not an answer.
G48.today: The simulation exposes its state and an outcome (sim/src/lib.rs:3131) and keeps no log of events; TD.13 plans one outside the checksum and TD.17 the result. Screens v3 hard-codes one moment and one tip per outcome (screens_main.js:637-638), and its replay button only plays a sound (:626). Every tip is headed 'The Archivist · try this' (screens_main.markup.html:843), which makes it one of §15.3's Archivist's tips rather than the result's own row, and the Clean tip, 'Kofi's universe is two realms deep. Same crew, a bigger haul.', suggests another target instead of following from its moment.

options.label: The drafted rule; the tip is the result's own row

The three-second replay is the three seconds ending on that tick. The tip comes from a content table keyed by the moment's cause, never a purchase, in a row labelled 'Try this', which is §15.3's 'One thing to try', not one of the Archivist's tips.

G70.today: server/src/matchmaking.mjs traceable() (lines 157-169) opens a Trace for a validated raid that was not foiled and was not cut by the raider's week cap. The week-cap condition (line 165) carries out your answer to G20 (C: raids past the twentieth pay no haul); server/test/service.test.mjs:325 pins it ('no Trace opened for the raider by a raid that took nothing') and server/README.md:133 states it. Screens v3's defence log agrees on 'not foiled' (screens_meta.js:592): Kofi's raid, which got out, and Marta's, a Partial the design tags 'HELD' (G69), offer a Trace; Ines's and Aiko's, where no loot got out, offer none. TD.66 offers Trace for each raid traceable() returns.

B is the rule a defender can check from the outcome alone, at the cost of a Trace against a raid that paid nothing. C57.question: Does the heist draw one guard's vision cone at a time, as §21.12 says, or the cone of every guard the crew can see, as §12.6 and §21.6 say?
C57.why_it_matters: v3.6 says both. §12.6 keeps 'the vision cones and awareness of guards the crew can see' always on screen, and §21.6 has 'a soft fan of light' show each guard's cone. §21.12 draws the selected guard's cone and only the facing of the others, because 'Five overlapping cones on a phone is noise', with sharp edges and no gradients. Your fix brief asks that 'Every visible guard shows its vision cone and an awareness meter' (screen-review.md:387, and :125). That is intent, not an answer.
C57.today: The client's flat heist view draws one guard's cone, the first guard on its feet unless another is selected (client/scripts/realm_view.gd:33). Screens v3's heist draws the focused guard's full cone and the others' facing (docs/analysis/screens-v3/screens-heist-result.md §1.2). TD.17 and TD.42 build §21.12's reading, with the other one token away.

options.consequences: Every guard's reach is in view at once, as your fix brief asks. With several guards in view the cones overlap, which §21.12 calls noise on a phone.

recommendation.rationale: §21.12 is the section written for this question, with its reason and its source, and the build and the design both draw it. Every visible guard still shows its awareness, so the half of §12.6 that warns the player holds. B is what your fix brief asks for; choose it if seeing every reach at once matters more than a clear screen.
